It consumes less memory than a single high-resolution uniform grid for sparse scenes but more than a BVH for highly clustered scenes.
*   **Strengths:** Handles non-uniform primitive distributions robustly; fast construction for dynamic scenes; SIMD-friendly traversal.
*   **Limitations:** Inferior traversal performance compared to optimized static scene structures; resolution limited to $256^3$ per cell; requires conservative pre-allocation of reference array.
*   **When to Use:** Dynamic scenes with non-uniform primitive distributions where fast construction is critical.
*   **When Not to Use:** Static scenes where maximum traversal performance is required; scenes with very high-resolution sub-grids needed.
It is a member of a class of hierarchical grids introduced by Jevans and Wyvill [JW89].

The method was developed to address the limitations of uniform grids on GPUs, specifically the "teapot in a stadium problem" where uniform grids fail to eliminate intersection candidates in sparse regions.
The construction algorithm generalizes the sort-based uniform grid construction by Kalojanov and Slusallek [KS09] to handle multiple sub-grids of varying resolutions in a single parallel sort.
